payload.body: The spectral kurtosis is the kurtosis (fourth standardized moment) of the spectral power distribution across frequency bins. Parameters: (1) the power-spectrum over which kurtosis is computed, (2) the normalization reference (typically the mean power squared). Computation: kurtosis = E[(P - μ)^4] / E[(P - μ)^2]^2 where P is the power spectrum and μ is its mean. The measure detects impulsive or non-stationary components in a signal by identifying frequency bins with heavy-tailed power distributions. The construct persists as a single scalar value per analyzed segment. Display: scalar, typically expressed in decibels. [formal: kurtosis spectralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: Tempo-estimation infers the beat rate of a periodic audio signal in beats per minute (BPM). Parameters: (1) the input audio signal or its envelope/attack-decay representation, (2) the analysis window duration over which tempo is estimated, (3) the BPM search range [min_bpm, max_bpm] typically [30, 300]. Computation: extract an onset/energy envelope, compute an autocorrelation or beat-spectrum over candidate BPM lags, select the peak within the search range as the estimated tempo. The construct persists as a single scalar BPM value per analyzed segment. Display: scalar in beats per minute, typically rounded to the nearest integer. [formal: estimatio temporis | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: The onset-envelope is a non-negative real-valued function of time representing the temporal strength of acoustic onsets in an audio signal. Parameters: (1) the input audio signal, (2) the analysis frame rate (samples per second or frames per second), (3) the onset detection function (e.g., spectral flux, energy difference, phase deviation) used to compute raw onset strength, (4) optional smoothing window length for post-processing. Computation: compute the onset detection function frame-by-frame, apply median or exponential smoothing to suppress spurious detections, optionally normalize to [0, 1]. The construct persists as a per-sample or per-frame vector synchronized with the input signal. Display: waveform or scalar trace aligned with audio time. [formal: envelopeum inceptionis | substrate: matter | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
